text: 你匆匆穿过迷雾笼罩的街道，躲进教堂。你进门时，门发出令人难以忍受的吱呀声，因此你不可能悄无声息地溜进去。
你发现自己身处一间宽敞的礼拜堂，两侧排列着手工雕刻的长椅。长椅一排排延伸，直到前方的讲坛，牧师通常会在那里主持礼拜。雾气滤过的日光正从彩绘玻璃窗间逐渐消退，你意识到现在并非通常举行礼拜的时间。教堂在非礼拜时段也对公众开放，但里面只有你和阿米莉娅。她坐在前排，低着头祈祷。
你坐到她旁边时，她没有抬眼看你。你坐了一会儿，给她时间做完祷告。你需要从她那里打听消息，但也尊重她的虔诚信仰。
最后，她睁开眼看向你，轻轻叹了口气。她看起来有些紧张，脸色也变得苍白。“你、你想要什么？你不该在这里。”

en.title: Alone Against the Tide · 164
text: You hurry through the shrouded streets and take refuge in the church. The door creaks abominably as you enter, so there’s no chance of slipping in unnoticed.

You find yourself in a large chapel, with hand-carved pews flanking you on either side. These continue for several rows until they reach a pulpit from which the priest would normally conduct services. With the last of the fog-filtered daylight fading through the stained-glass windows, you are aware that these are not the hours of a typical service. The church is open to the public during off-times, but the sole occupants are yourself and Amelia, who’s taken a seat in the front row and is praying with her head bowed.
She does not lift her gaze as you take a seat next to her. You sit for a minute and allow her time to finish her prayers. You need information from her, but you’re respectful of her devotions.
Finally, she opens her eyes and looks at you, sighing softly as she does so. She looks somewhat nervous, and the color drains from her face. “W-what is it you want? You’re not supposed to be here.”
